newsitem.title: USA: Macedonia seeks to keep U.N. peace troops.
newsitem.headline: Macedonia seeks to keep U.N. peace troops.

text.p: Macedonian Defence Minister Blagoj Hnadijski met with U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen on Friday as part of an effort to keep U.N. peacekeeping troops in Macedonia.
Cohen was open to the request, saying "We will discuss ways in which we can hopefully continue our presence into the future."
The United States has about 500 peacekeeping troops in the Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia, about half the U.N. peace force there.

Hnadijski told reporters before the meeting: "Our position is there are a dozen various reasons why we ... will ask the United Nations, the Security Council, to extend the mission after the 31st of May."
He said Macedonia had been able to keep peace despite war in neighbouring Bosnia largely because of U.S. support.
Cohen wants all U.S. troops out of Bosnia when the current NATO peacekeeping mission ends in mid-1998 but was open to extending the Macedonia peace mission beyond May 31.

When the Security Council last November renewed the mandate of the U.N. Preventive Deployment Force (UNPREDEP) in Macedonia until May 31, it also called for a phased reduction in its size, to be completed by April 30.

UNPREDEP, which includes some the U.S. troops and a similar number from Nordic countries, was originally deployed to prevent conflicts elsewhere in the former Yugoslavia from spilling over into Macedonia.
